conventions.convention: Likelihoods use specified pointwise density versions relative to a common dominating measure. Parameter sets are nonempty; profiling uses suprema, with the global supremum required to be finite and strictly positive. A zero profile ratio gives q=+∞.

Larger real-valued statistics are more extreme; the upper tail includes equality. The calibration law is explicitly supplied, and the definition asserts neither automatic type-I error control nor a posterior probability of the null.
CLb and CLs+b use the same inclusive upper-tail event, ordered toward incompatibility with signal plus background. CLs is defined only when CLb>0; exclusion uses the strict inequality CLs<α.

The ATLAS 99% compatibility result concerns the linear fit without di-Higgs inputs: 47 fitted directions and 39 other directions fixed to zero. Its global calibration is not reconstructed or identified with coefficient-interval calibration.

The multiboson table reports single-coefficient linear-plus-quadratic intervals in TeV⁻² with all other coefficients fixed to zero. Rounded 95% labels retain the source's 95.4% threshold convention; simultaneous six-parameter coverage is not asserted.
The tau-search significance is local to GG(1300,1200), and mass reaches are specific to the stated simplified spectra, branching fractions, channels and analysis strategies.

load_bearing.statement: For specified dominated densities and observed s, assume 0<M_s<+∞, where M_s is the global likelihood supremum. Define M_s(ψ) as the nuisance-coordinate supremum, λ_s(ψ)=M_s(ψ)/M_s, and q_s(ψ)=−2 log λ_s(ψ) when λ_s(ψ)>0, with q_s(ψ)=+∞ otherwise. No maximizing parameter or sampling calibration is asserted.

For a real statistic T with measurable upper tails and a supplied calibration probability measure Q0, define p0(s)=Q0({t:t≥T(s)}). For a simple null, exact calibration is the pushforward of its sampling law by T. Composite-null and asymptotic calibration procedures must supply their nuisance treatment and approximation assumptions.

For supplied background-only and signal-plus-background laws and R_x={y:T(y)≥T(x)}, define CLb(x)=Pb(R_x) and CLs+b(x)=Ps+b(R_x). When CLb(x)>0, define CLs(x)=CLs+b(x)/CLb(x); the supplied analysis excludes at threshold α when CLs(x)<α.

concerns.concern: Setup calls the discarded 21 principal-component directions ones 'with no sensitivity'. The source instead applies a finite sensitivity cutoff and describes the omitted directions as insufficiently constrained; zero sensitivity is stronger. See [CMS paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.02958v2), §7, printed p.23.

Procedure names the anti-kt algorithm, a 'medium identification working point', the fake-factor method and machine-learning strategies without defining their operative maps or identifying exact earlier definitions. In particular, its deps contain only statistical suppliers. The primary source supplies reconstruction and fake-factor definitions in §§5–7, but the item gives only broad section links. Supply the relevant definitions or precise source-input interfaces and explicit limits, as the multiboson item does.
